items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: Wonderful. I always liked to play with Turk, wonderful fella he was to me, anyhow.

ctx.x: The cane, yeah, one of the canes. Lot of cane growing. Man went back there and cut one of them stalks off there and come out there and Bechet set down there and on that track, and he cut that keys, cut that -- I don't know how he done that, but he did fix the key to put on that clarinet, and cut him out a reed, and put it on there and blowing his head off. Come in there start to blowing, oh Lord, that was it.

Okay, that's great. But let's just try to finish up this session, Tootie, with tracing your career up to today, then. All right, so we're having a lovely time, we've spoken about some of the instruments, now, after you worked with Earl Hines, you worked for a bit with Turk Murphy.
